chunks: As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥukaym, from Mūsā ibn Bakr, from Abī Maryam; and by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā and Muʿāwiyah, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Ribāṭ, from Abī Maryam al-Anṣārī, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Regarding a woman who killed a man, he said: “She is to be killed, and her guardian pays the remainder of the wealth.” And in the narration of Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb: “the remainder of the blood-money.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: This narration is anomalous; none narrated it other than Abī Maryam al-Anṣārī, even if it is repeated in the books in various places. Along with that, it contradicts all the reports and the apparent meaning of the Qur'an.
Allah, the Exalted, said: “And We prescribed for them therein that a life is for a life, and an eye for an eye” — the verse.

So the ruling was given that a life is for a life, and nothing else was mentioned along with it. All the narrations have clearly stated that a person does not incur liability beyond his own life, and that nothing is due upon her heirs if they kill her. Thus, when this narration comes in contradiction to what we have mentioned, acting upon it should be abandoned.

And no one may say that the verse is only reporting what Allah, the Exalted, prescribed for the Jews in the Torah, and that it does not indicate that this is our ruling. For although the verse includes that it was prescribed for the people of the Torah, its ruling is operative among us; what has been narrated indicates that:

key_terms.أَوْلِيَائِهَا: her heirs or legal guardians in the context of retaliation
key_terms.النَّفْسَ بِالنَّفْسِ: the legal principle of life-for-life retaliation
key_terms.الْأَخْبَارِ: the hadith reports used as evidence in legal reasoning
key_terms.الْعَمَلُ بِهَا: acting upon the report as a basis for legal ruling
key_terms.بَقِيَّةَ الدِّيَةِ: the remainder of the blood-money said in the disputed report to be paid
key_terms.شَاذَّةٌ: anomalous; a report judged irregular and not fit for legal reliance here
key_terms.ظَاهِرِ الْقُرْآنِ: the apparent, outward meaning of the Qur'anic wording

ai.seo_question: Why did al-Ṭūsī consider the narration requiring payment from a woman's guardian in qiṣāṣ to be anomalous?
ai.summary: This passage discusses a narration concerning qiṣāṣ in the case of a woman who kills a man, then rejects that report as anomalous and contrary to other hadith reports and the apparent wording of the Qur'an. The argument given is that the principle "a life for a life" establishes retaliation without additional financial liability upon her heirs.
